tldr: On Nov 2 the VIAS paper tested activation steering, adding vectors to internal activations at generation time, to make LLM agents follow several organisational values at once. A Nov 13 paper argued that steering every token pushes representations off-distribution and proposed per-token gating that follows the generation trajectory.
whats_new: A Nov 19 paper argues that RL post-training of diffusion transformers amounts to activation steering, linking a costly training step to an inference-time intervention.
why_it_matters: Activation steering is a behavior control that needs no fine-tuning run, so if it can isolate values, gate per token, or stand in for RL gains, teams get a cheaper lever for compliance and quality tuning on open-weight models.

beats.headline: VIAS isolates per-value steering vectors for organisational compliance
SAE steering moves from every token to trajectory-aware gating
beats.summary: Targets the off-distribution drift that always-on steering causes.

beats.headline: RL post-training in diffusion transformers recast as activation steering

open_questions: Does VIAS keep several value vectors from interfering when they are applied together?
How much generation quality does trajectory-aware gating recover compared with steering every token?
Can a steering vector reproduce the RL post-training gains in diffusion transformers without running RL?
Does any result here carry over between text LLMs and diffusion transformers?
take_for_builders: If you steer an open-weight model for policy compliance, measure output quality with steering on versus off per token before shipping; always-on steering is the failure mode the Nov 13 paper targets.
